authorization: User requested completion, green checks, merge and verified publication.
intent: Resolve Android streaming ASR linkage by preserving static sentencepiece intent through its legacy CMake option boundary.

observed_failure.head: dbf61eccd0d0b6af7f39b853825a3b066dc4f11d
observed_failure.scope: Both API34 and API36 jobs failed native APK packaging before device tests.
observed_failure.cause: Pinned simple-sentencepiece v0.7 resets policy to CMake3.12 and option(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ON) discards a normal OFF value, creating a hidden-symbol shared dependency.

changes: Scope the CMP0077 default and normal static selection inside a dependency helper while preserving the caller normal/cache/default values.
Reject any unexpected non-static target and retain the existing cstdint compatibility include.
Exercise the production helper at the nested legacy option boundary, across fresh and repeated configuration and a forced shared-target negative control.

android_link_proof.baseline: Both actual pinned-source builds reproduce the two undefined APIs with a shared target.
android_link_proof.fixed: Both actual pinned-source builds produce a static dependency, successfully link the consumer, resolve both APIs and have no sentencepiece shared-library dependency.
android_link_proof.scope: Actual pinned source Android NDK compile/link for the two application ABIs, not the complete app.

validation.independent_review: No actionable blocker; frozen source, pinned inputs, baseline failures and both corrected ABI link proofs independently verified. Caller settings and all release gates preserved.

preserved: All dependency/model hashes and provider choices.
Caller CMake settings, required host tests and cancellation/retirement controls.
Every existing CI gate, release version and physical qualification limitation.
limits: Focused NDK link verification does not execute the full app, native speech models or physical devices.
Full exact-head Android/device/native checks and merged-main checks remain required before publication.
